name: Anirban Chatterjee
bio: Anirban Chatterjee leads AI strategy and partnerships at Sonar, working at the intersection of AI product, go-to-market, and developer code quality as software teams adopt AI agents.

positions.claim: AI coding tools produce a productivity gain that decays after roughly three months while leaving a persistent increase in static analysis warnings and code complexity.
The quality gap between AI-generated code and required code quality is acceptable for low-criticality projects but must be closed by humans for high-criticality ones.
Human code review is an unreliable backstop because people accept confidently-wrong AI output nearly 80% of the time.
Rubber-stamping of AI-generated code is already widespread in most organizations.
You should not use the same AI that wrote the code to validate it; verification must use a different methodology than generation.
No single verification technique suffices — computational/static and LLM-driven review must be combined.
Software, unlike code, is not provable, because requirements, scale, and user behavior create unpredictable interactions.
Verification must run inside the inner agentic loop, not only in CI/CD, so defects are fixed before propagating into subsequent loops.
Claude Sonnet 4.6 scores well on correctness and task-solving, but Opus is the better choice when maintainability, security, or low complexity are priorities.
Dumping an entire codebase into an agent's context is counterproductive; selectively supplied context reduces thrashing and token burn.
Organizations should standardize on a single independent multi-layered verification platform across all teams, projects, and AI coding tools to eliminate blind spots.
Agents should be given the agency and tooling to remediate their own verification findings rather than routing every fix to a human.
